geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the current setback stack into a sectionally legible dominant mass while preserving the bent-bar ancestry.
Use a folded profile to support the neighborhood brief with a clearer roof/section relation.
Preserve the long-axis continuity of the primary mass.
Introduce a courtyard-based public void as the main access-side ground response.
Scale the void to read as meaningful public space.
Align the opening to the verified access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Retain the bent-ribbon hierarchy but convert the top-level step logic into a more program-legible section family instead of a generic setback stack.
A folded section better supports neighborhood living by making the roof/section read as inhabitable, not merely tiered.
Keep the dominant bar continuity along the long axis so the gesture remains one readable mass.
Add a public court/void to articulate the access edge and create a legible ground threshold.
Make the void large enough to register as usable public open space rather than a token notch.
Open the court toward the verified site access side to strengthen the street-facing threshold.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single gesture in all views: a bent, stepping ribbon with readable hierarchy and no obvious multi-view collision. The silhouette is competent but the step mass reads more as a formal terracing device than as a clearly inhabited public section. The main weakness is program fit: for neighborhood living, the mass does not yet provide a convincing active street threshold or a sufficiently public void/court. The verified access edge is present only weakly as a perimeter relationship; it should become a clearer carve, notch, or courtyard opening aligned to the access side. Compared with the references, the candidate resonates most with the terraced and courtyard-based neighborhood precedents, but it remains too sealed and too object-like at ground level. Repair integrity is strong because the form is legible and not obviously over-clipped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion/cultural and more openly carved than the candidate; useful for void and threshold, not for copying the curved parapet language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a pronounced central void and a clear bridge/threshold condition can support neighborhood program well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; its tower-podium scale should not be transferred.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A multi-part campus-like composition can still read as one public precinct when courts and setbacks organize the whole.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More transparent and site-porous than the candidate; the candidate currently lacks comparable public ground porosity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long horizontal massing with a courtyard-like opening and a gently sloped roof can keep the ground active while maintaining a calm upper datum.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and less sectionally articulated; terrace logic needs a stronger public ground relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, spread-out masses can create a coherent neighborhood section where roofs, ramps, and voids produce usable public open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more rectilinear and interlocked, whereas the candidate is a single bent/stepped ribbon; only the void-and-hierarchy principle transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking masses and a large central void can give a neighborhood building clear hierarchy and legible circulation around a court.

warnings: Parcel containment is presumed satisfied from the visible diagram, but the access-edge response is still semantically weak.
The form is coherent, but the public threshold is underdeveloped relative to the neighborhood_living brief.
Do not read the stepped silhouette as automatically program-appropriate; it needs a clearer ground void or entry seam.
